html:
October 19, 2026

Russian missiles and drones cut power to half a million Ukrainians as Kyiv says it got no early warning

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region and more than 200 drones across Ukraine overnight, striking 28 substations and other energy facilities as well as a medical clinic, a school, a metro station and residential buildings. President Volodymyr Zelensky said electricity, heat and running water were cut to more than half a million people and that a 21-year-old woman was killed in Kyiv. Zelensky said Ukraine received no early warning from its partners before the first wave, though the air force said information arrived before a second wave, too late for sirens. President Trump says Washington has not stopped sharing intelligence, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he had no information about the attack; Zelensky also cited a severe shortage of Patriot systems and continued restrictions on military-grade Starlink.

Trump waives Russia sanctions and strikes diesel deal as envoys float European return to Russian gas

tags: politics, war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual, @carolinegleich

President Trump signed an executive order exempting Russia from sanctions passed by Congress with bipartisan support, following a call with Vladimir Putin that also produced a deal to buy Russian diesel. Peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have separately proposed that Europe resume purchases of Russian natural gas as part of a Ukraine settlement, raising the idea with Ukrainian and European officials including Zelensky in Kyiv; German officials pushed back sharply, with security adviser Guenter Sautter opposing it at talks in Florida. Ukraine stopped transporting Russian gas in January 2025 and the EU has pledged to end all Russian gas imports by next year, with Russian gas down to 13 percent of EU imports from 45 percent in 2021. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called the sanctions waiver a gift to Putin, and critics also point to Trump saying Ukraine needs a new president, slowed Starlink service for Ukrainian drones, and Russian assistance to Iran in targeting American troops.

Putin proposes a three-way summit with Trump and Xi on ending the Ukraine war

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Putin floated a meeting with Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping next month during an October 9 phone call, with terms aimed at favoring Moscow, according to people familiar with the discussions. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed talks are under way but said there is no clear understanding yet of the meeting or its agenda. The Kremlin suggested holding it alongside the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19; a senior U.S. official said Trump has not agreed but could be receptive, and Chinese representatives signaled they would not object. The proposed summit would exclude Zelensky, raising concerns in Europe that Ukraine's future could be negotiated without Kyiv.

Ukraine launches one of its largest drone attacks of the year as Trump turns on Zelensky

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russia's defense ministry said it shot down 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday. The St. Petersburg Oil Terminal was hit and left burning, and an Ozon logistics center and a VK data center in the Leningrad region were also struck; local authorities reported one person killed, five wounded and homes damaged. In a Truth Social post, Trump said great progress was being made in peace talks but said Zelensky does not want to end the war and probably never did. Zelensky has said Washington siding with Russia would be a historic mistake and that sanctions relief amounts to more support for Russian aggression.

Trump endorses Netanyahu days before Israel's election

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews

President Trump issued what he called a complete and total endorsement of Benjamin Netanyahu on October 18, ahead of Israel's October 27 parliamentary election, calling him a Great Warrior Prime Minister and praising his role in the U.S.-Israeli offensive against Iran. In the Truth Social letter Trump said Iran had been systematically destroyed militarily and financially and that the United States would soon finish the job, adding that if Israel elected anyone other than Netanyahu, America would have to do the work itself. Netanyahu thanked Trump on X, writing that together they would complete the mission. Polls indicate Netanyahu's coalition could fall short of the seats needed to govern, and a deadlock could trigger another election with him staying on in a caretaker role.

Houthi strikes push Riyadh tower to send workers home as Saudi Arabia recruits foreign fighters

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Management at the 99-story Kingdom Centre in Riyadh told office employees to work remotely until further notice after the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two drones over the Riyadh area, a third over the Eastern Province and two ballistic missiles in the south. The directive follows an October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, severe disruption to airport operations and extended remote learning in Riyadh schools. The Wall Street Journal reports Saudi Arabia is recruiting foreign fighters to back its Yemeni allies as the attacks expose the kingdom's military limitations, with a Saudi official calling the Houthis a global threat requiring a global response. Analysts say the Houthis can absorb coalition airstrikes while continuing deep strikes on soft Saudi targets.

Egypt's parliament delays vote on authorizing military support for Saudi Arabia

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Lawmakers adjourned a second closed-door session and pushed the vote to October 26 to extend debate over President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request for authority to defend Saudi Arabia if asked. Under Egypt's constitution, sending the armed forces on a combat mission abroad requires a two-thirds majority after consultation with the National Defence Council. The Egyptian Social Democratic Party instructed its lawmakers to abstain, saying parliament had not received enough information on the mission's objectives, scope, duration, cost or risks, and Al-Azhar's grand imam called for urgent mediation by Arab and Muslim leaders. Saudi Arabia holds a $5.3 billion deposit at Egypt's central bank due this month, and Egypt's stock index closed 0.4 percent higher after earlier falls tied to concerns over military involvement.

Airstrike on Yemeni house kills at least nine as civil war reignites

tags: war
sources: @oafnation_actual

A strike hit a house in the Sahar district of northern Saada province on Sunday, killing at least nine people including five children and two women, according to Houthi-run Health Ministry spokesman Anees al-Asbahi. Nineteen others were wounded, including 11 children, some in critical condition; the figures have not been independently verified. The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia, and there was no immediate comment from Riyadh. The strike was one of several over the weekend that killed or wounded more than 30 people, as Houthi ballistic missile strikes on Yemeni government forces killed at least 53 and the Saudi-led coalition launched a major offensive near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Tugboat struck off the UAE amid a surge of attacks on commercial shipping

tags: war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

A southbound tug traveling northeast of Khor Fakkan was hit by two projectiles of unknown origin on Sunday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said. The vessel was damaged but continued its voyage and one crew member suffered a minor injury, with authorities investigating and vessels advised to transit with caution. UKMTO's weekly report recorded 12 attacks in the week ending October 16, including 10 in the Strait of Hormuz, and warned the true number may be higher because many targeted vessels do not report incidents. A day earlier, an LNG carrier's armed security team fired warning shots at a skiff that fired on the tanker off Yemen.

Suspected drone over Lithuania forces residents to shelter and closes an airport

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Residents in northern and central Lithuania sheltered for about an hour on Sunday morning after a suspected drone entered the country's airspace. NATO Baltic Air Policing jets scrambled but could not visually identify the object through cloud cover and did not fire on it, and Kaunas airport was briefly closed. Debris believed to be from the drone was found near the village of Juodzionys and some of it struck a civilian vehicle, Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said, adding the object appeared to have come from Poland, though a Polish defense ministry spokesperson said radar did not confirm a crossing. Ukraine's foreign ministry said the incident may have been caused by Russian electronic warfare diverting a drone off course, and President Gitanas Nauseda said Russia's war was spilling onto NATO's eastern flank; it came a day after Romanian F-16s shot down two unauthorized drones over the Black Sea.

Judge hauls Trump lawyers into court over East Potomac Park golf course plan

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Judge Ana Reyes held a testy hearing in federal court in Washington over President Trump's plan to redevelop a golf course at East Potomac Park, forcing top administration officials to testify and at one point asking Justice Department lawyers to raise their hands if they agreed with a filing made the previous night. A week earlier, Trump's lawyers had told the court he had no concrete plan for the site; White House press secretary Katie Zachariah then published a photograph of herself with Trump and the plan in the Oval Office, and Trump subsequently posted the plan on Truth Social and called Reyes a lunatic judge. Democracy Forward lawyers are arguing the case against the redevelopment. Critics contrast the project with the administration's handling of the Epstein files, the war and the cost of living.

BBC seeks Jack Smith deposition in Trump's $10 billion lawsuit

tags: legal, media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

In a court filing, the BBC said it has asked former special counsel Jack Smith to sit for a deposition in the $10 billion lawsuit Trump brought over the broadcaster's coverage of January 6. The BBC argues Smith, who spent years investigating Trump over the events of that day, is fair game given the subject of the suit. Trump opposes the testimony, while Smith has indicated he is willing and able to appear.

ICE fires thousands after record hiring surge, leaving ex-officers blacklisted

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Between July 2025 and May 2026, ICE onboarded 12,000 new agents and officers in the largest hiring surge in U.S. federal law enforcement history, eliminating upper age caps, lowering the minimum applicant age to 18, offering $50,000 signing bonuses and cutting training and vetting standards. The agency is now losing roughly 5,000 personnel by mid-2026, with terminations and firings accounting for 73 percent of all separations, compared with 16 percent in previous years. Former officers say they are effectively blacklisted afterward, with one recently terminated deportation officer saying he can never work in federal law enforcement again and that local police departments will not hire him with ICE on his resume.

Treasury prepares financial penalties for borrowers in student loan default

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Treasury Department officials are preparing to impose financial penalties on millions of Americans currently in default on federal student loans, with private debt collectors hired to carry out collection, according to reporting cited in the post. The penalties could begin as soon as next year. The plan is not final and officials are still working on ways to limit the impact on vulnerable borrowers, and it could be delayed; any announcement is expected to come after the midterm elections.

Albania's Supreme Court set on fire as anti-corruption protests spread

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Supreme Court of Albania was set on fire as student-led anti-corruption protests expanded across the country. The demonstrations began after the government allowed Jared Kushner to take over part of Albania for a Trump- and Kushner-backed development project, prompting widespread outrage among residents. Protesters are now calling on the prime minister to resign, and daily demonstrations have continued for months, broadening into a nationwide movement against government corruption.

Trump officials hire personal lawyers ahead of possible congressional investigations

tags: politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Administration officials from cabinet secretaries to midlevel staffers are calling law firms to line up personal counsel in case Democrats win one or both chambers in the November 3 midterms, according to the Wall Street Journal. Lawyers say inquiries began sporadically in June and have picked up since, with concern about probes ranging from alleged pay-to-play pardons to the Kennedy Center renovation and Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding. Officials are shopping top firms and smaller conservative boutiques including Torridon Law, whose partners include former Attorney General William Barr, and conflict-of-interest rules mean one firm is unlikely to represent several staffers at once. If Democrats take the House, lawyers said, the investigations could interfere with the president's agenda through his final two years.

Utah rally targets redistricting and a data center approved without public comment

tags: politics, tech
sources: @carolinegleich

At a No Kings rally in Salt Lake City, a speaker described receiving threatening messages telling her to leave Utah; the sender was identified with help from her community and is being prosecuted. The speech accused state leaders of changing rules after losing, redrawing fair maps and packing courts, and pointed to an unelected board, MIDA, approving a data center larger than Manhattan after 1,100 people turned out and none were allowed to speak. It noted that Utah Senate President Stuart Adams, who chaired that board, lost his first primary in 16 years in June, alongside defeats for Trevor Lee and Dan McKay. Voters were urged to return ballots by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3 and to write the last four digits of a driver license or Social Security number on the envelope.

Trump signs executive order creating women's health task force and NIH division

tags: health, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The order establishes a White House Women's Health Task Force and a new Women's Health Division at the National Institutes of Health, signed at a Rose Garden ceremony with First Lady Melania Trump, who pressed the administration for months on the issue. The task force will be led by White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and held its first meeting Monday afternoon. The order directs research funds toward diseases that disproportionately affect women, uses AI to speed medical research, moves therapies from labs to patients faster and expands education. The new division will not replace the NIH Office of Research on Women's Health, which has operated since 1990.

National Guardsman shot in Washington while breaking up a street fight

tags: policing, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Seven or eight Guard members intervened in a street fight near Eastern Market late Sunday night when a man opened fire and pointed his weapon toward them, police said. Three Guard members returned fire, striking the suspect in the abdomen, and one Guardsman was shot in the leg. Both injuries were described as non-life-threatening and the suspect was arrested.

Five SAS soldiers cleared after three-year murder investigation over Syria raid

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Five British SAS soldiers were under a murder investigation for nearly three years following a 2022 operation against ISIS in Syria. They reportedly returned to combat while the investigation remained open, and prosecutors declined to bring charges in 2025. The SAS Regimental Association is criticizing how the soldiers were treated during the process.

Yale lab estimates at least 35,000 Ukrainian children abducted by Russia

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Yale School of Public Health Humanitarian Research Lab estimates at least 35,000 children have been taken from families and orphanages in Ukraine, placed in re-education camps and adopted out to Russian families, with older children forced to fight against Ukraine. The exact number is impossible to establish. A former USAID expert described Russia's conduct in Ukraine as WWII-level atrocities. The post ties the issue to the November 3 midterms and to the volume of references to Trump's name in the Epstein files released so far.

Fire and fatalities reported at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Defence Minister David McGuinty confirmed multiple fatalities and significant injuries after a serious incident and fire Saturday afternoon at CFB Wainwright in Alberta, about 130 miles southeast of Edmonton. The municipal district said the blaze spread rapidly in high winds and firefighters worked to keep it from reaching residential areas, with the RCMP called around 4 p.m. local time and set to investigate. Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed a serious incident and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called it significant and tragic, affecting many military personnel. Unconfirmed reports say an explosion preceded the fire, and the cause has not been released.

European salmon farms turn to chicken byproducts as fishmeal prices soar

tags: environment, markets
sources: @groundnews

Norway's Lerøy Seafood Group has introduced poultry-based feed across its salmon farms and Mowi, the world's largest salmon producer, plans to follow, reversing a practice long avoided over consumer reaction. Traditional fishmeal prices have nearly doubled in two years because of declining fish stocks and rising demand, while poultry-based feed costs less than half as much and includes chicken bones, organs and other parts not used for human consumption. European retailers have historically restricted poultry-fed salmon, but labeling laws do not require producers to disclose feed ingredients, leaving consumers unaware of the change.
